## Reasoning
(1) I checked the git history for `CustomPieChart.java` using `git log --follow`, which showed the file only has two commits total: the fix commit (`04139db`) and one prior commit (`878f010`) that created the file.

(2) I then viewed the diff of `878f010`, which shows the file was newly added (`new file mode`) with the exact same broken code that the fix commit corrects: an anonymous `PieRadarChartTouchListener` subclass body containing a bare `if (h != null && !h.equalTo(mLastHighlighted)) { ... }` block with no enclosing method declaration (`protected void performHighlight(Highlight h, MotionEvent e) { ... }`). This is invalid Java syntax — a statement cannot appear directly inside a class body — which explains the "fix ci error" commit message (the CI build would fail to compile).

(3) The evidence is unambiguous: the buggy code block is byte-for-byte identical between the newly-added file in `878f010` and the "before" side of the fix diff in `04139db`. There is no intermediate commit that touched this file, so the bug was introduced in its entirety when the file was first created in `878f010`.

There is no meaningful uncertainty here — the file's complete history consists of exactly these two commits, and the diffs match precisely.
